reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) describes strain-rate sensitivity and dislocation-mediated deformation in other high-entropy alloys, but none of it directly addresses the Co-free FeNiCrMn system, its as-solidified microstructure, or the specific adiabatic shear band mechanism proposed. The premises are therefore extrapolations rather than claims supported by the cited passages.
premises: Severe lattice distortions and restricted dislocation mobility are inherent in the single-phase, as-solidified FeNiCrMn microstructure.
At low strain rates, thermally activated dislocation glide controls deformation and work hardening.
At high strain rates, rapid dislocation accumulation leads to localized adiabatic shear band formation.
This dislocation-based mechanism governs the dynamic strength–ductility balance in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The dynamic yield strength increases with strain rate due to dislocation drag and shear band formation.
